prototype.headline: No OAuth app needed to start: connect through Composio's managed Notion app.

production.headline: Production use follows the same review process; timing varies.

verdict.confidence: Medium: creation and token flow steps are documented, but review timing and managed‑track usage are uncertain.
verdict.summary: Notion offers a self‑serve public connection that requires a workspace‑owner review before the auth URL is released. The OAuth flow itself is standard and documented, but the provider does not publish limits, paid‑tier requirements, or PKCE rules.

stages.name: Connect through Composio's managed Notion app

steps.text: Create a Composio session for your user. Do not pass an auth config for notion, so the managed app is used.
Send the user a Connect Link. They approve on Notion's consent screen, which shows Composio's app name.
Run one test tool call to confirm the connection works.

stages.name: Determine if a public connection (OAuth) is needed

steps.text: If your integration must be installed by other Notion users, you need a public connection (OAuth). Otherwise use an internal connection.

stages.name: Create a public connection in Notion

steps.text: Log into https://app.notion.com/developers/connections as a workspace owner and click **New public connection**.
Fill in the connection name, description, and **Redirect URI(s)**. Note: the redirect URI cannot be changed after creation.
After saving the connection, click **Submit for review**. The **Authorization URL** field will be populated only after the review is approved.
From the connection’s **Configuration** tab, copy the **Client ID**, **Client Secret**, and the generated **Authorization URL**.

stages.name: Agent creates a Connect Link (managed OAuth)

steps.text: Using Composio’s managed Notion OAuth app, draft the Connect Link with the collected credentials and the redirect URI.
Generate the link, share it with a test user, and poll the connection status until it becomes **ACTIVE**.

stages.name: Store access and refresh tokens securely

steps.text: When the user completes the flow, Notion returns `access_token` and `refresh_token` (see token endpoint). Store them in a secret manager or encrypted database.
Composio’s managed OAuth runtime automatically refreshes tokens using the same token endpoint with `grant_type=refresh_token`.
Monitor API errors (e.g., 401) and re‑run the token refresh flow if needed. If the connection is blocked, contact Notion support via the help center.

requirements: Workspace owner rights in Notion (required to create a public connection)
A valid HTTPS redirect URI that matches the one registered in the connection
Client ID and Client Secret obtained from the Notion Developer portal
Compliance with Notion’s Terms of Service
If you want Notion's MCP server rather than its API, that is a separate Composio toolkit (NOTION_MCP) with its own auth (k5).

blockers.issue: Review delay prevents obtaining the Authorization URL
blockers.whenItHits: After submitting the public connection for review
blockers.whatToDo: Wait for Notion to approve the connection; if the review exceeds a week, contact Notion support for status.

blockers.issue: Non‑owner cannot create a public connection
blockers.whenItHits: When a non‑owner attempts to access the Developer portal
blockers.whatToDo: Ask a workspace owner to create the connection or transfer ownership.

agentCanDo: Draft the Composio OAuth configuration values (client ID, secret, redirect URI)
Generate the Connect Link and poll connection status until ACTIVE
Run test API calls using the obtained access token
Handle token refresh automatically via the managed OAuth runtime
youMustDo: Create the public connection in Notion and submit it for review
Provide the client ID, client secret, and redirect URI to Composio
Store the access and refresh tokens securely in your own infrastructure
Monitor usage and handle any compliance or policy questions

claims.text: Public connections use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
You must be a workspace owner to create a public connection.
Redirect URI(s) are set in the OAuth configuration section and cannot be changed after creation.
The Authorization URL field populates after a public connection is submitted for review.
Calling https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with an invalid client_id redirects to a login page (302).
The token endpoint is https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token and returns an access_token and refresh_token.
Token exchange uses HTTP Basic Authentication with client_id:client_secret base64‑encoded.
Refreshing an access token uses the same token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token.
Composio provides a managed OAuth integration for Notion.
Composio's NOTION toolkit lists auth OAUTH2, API_KEY; Composio-managed OAuth available: yes.

composioTail: In the Composio dashboard go to Auth Configs, click Create Auth Config, select the toolkit and choose OAuth2.
Copy the redirect URI shown in the Composio dashboard and register it in the provider's app settings.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the provider app overview into the Composio auth config, and click Create.
Copy the resulting auth config ID (looks like ac_xxxx). Keep secrets out of source control.
Pass the auth config ID to your session: authConfigs: { [toolkit]: 'ac_xxxx' }. Toolkits not listed keep using Composio managed auth.
